body.p: Claims 1-11 are pending and stand rejected. Claim 1 has been amended. Claims 12-14 have been added.

The specification (paragraph [0005]) has been further amended to include additional subject matter from US Patent 10,173,292, the disclosure of which is incorporated into the specification by reference. No new matter is believed to be added.
Applicant's attorney wishes to thank the Examiner for his time during their telephone discussion on December 17, 2024.
Applicant's attorney agrees with the Examiner's Interview Summary. Applicant is providing the following summary of the interview under MPEP 713.04:
(A) Brief description of exhibit shown or demonstration conducted: None
(B) Identification of the claims discussed: Claims 1 and 11.
(C) Identification of the specific prior art discussed: U.S. Patent Application Pub Nos.
2020/0039662 Al, Descheemaeker and 2017/0251313 Al, Gustafsson.
(D) Identification of the principal proposed amendments of a substantive nature discussed:
Applicant's attorney and Examiner discussed that Applicant's attorney would consider making amendments to the claims to add the "wherein clause" language from Claim 1
of U.S. Patent 11,772,812 B1 into Claim 1 of the present application.
(E) General thrust of the principal arguments of applicant: Applicant did not present
arguments.
(F) General indication of other pertinent matters discussed: None
(G) General results or outcome of the interview: Applicant's attorney indicated that he
would likely be filing an RCE to make this amendment. It was agreed that the proposed
amendment would overcome the current rejections.
(H) Interview via electronic mail: N/A.
Claims 1-10 stand rejected on the grounds of nonstatutory obviousness-type double patenting as being unpatentable over Claims 1-10 of U.S. Patent 11,772,812.
Without admitting that the double patenting rejection is properly imposed, Applicant is submitting a terminal disclaimer herewith to obviate the double patenting rejection.
In view of the foregoing, Applicant respectfully requests that the double patent rejection be withdrawn.
Claims 1 and 11 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over
Descheemaeker (U.S. Patent Application 2020/0039662) in view of Gustafsson (U.S. Patent Application 2017/0251313).
Applicant respectfully requests that this rejection be reconsidered and withdrawn.

Although Applicant continues to believe that Claims 1 and 11 as filed are patentable, Applicant has amended Claim 1 to add the "wherein clause" language as discussed during the interview. As indicated in the Examiner's interview summary, it was agreed that the latter aspect of the proposed amendment would overcome the current rejections.

In view of the agreement that this amendment would overcome the current rejections, Applicant will not repeat Applicant's previous arguments in full regarding patentability of the claims over the combination of references, but will incorporate its prior arguments by reference herein and only make brief references thereto, and provide some supplementary information.

The magnets described in Descheemaeker are electromagnets which are a type of magnet in which the magnetic field is produced by an electric current. Electromagnets usually consist of a wire wound into a coil. An electromagnet requires a continuous supply of current to maintain the magnetic field. See article on electromagnets transmitted herewith. Applicant believes that the combination of references does not render the subject matter of Claim 1 obvious according to the guidance set out in MPEP 2143.01V and VI.
In view of the foregoing, it is respectfully requested that this rejection be reconsidered and withdrawn.

New Claims

New Claims 12-14 are dependent from Claim 1 and, therefore, should also be patentable over the combination of references in the final Office Action. In addition, Claims 12 and 13 are further distinguishable from the electromagnets described in the Descheemaeker reference. Permanent magnets differ from electromagnets in that permanent magnets maintain their magnetic properties in the absence of an inducing field or current. Permanent magnets have to be removed by a force greater than the magnetic force holding the magnets in place.
